baseline.rule: exhaustive cost-bounded scalar kernels and two-input predicates; finite inverse sample and polynomial seed templates separately declared

adaptive.allocation: identical expanded mutations in both arms; round robin equal attempts per family; rejected syntax retained

promotion.rule: subtrees of validated programs, any declared type with explicit free indices; rank by reuse*(cost-1), then canonical hash; exact expansion retained

selection.rule: Pareto front plus equal round-robin criterion queues, exact behavioral deduplication; no final data
selection.prime_baseline: index residues modulo 2 and 3; output buckets zero, one, negative real, other

data.final_seed_rule: OS entropy, drawn by evaluator only AFTER archive and fitted benchmark programs are sealed
data.arithmetic: Q and Q(i), exact; cancellation has no floating roundoff

calibration.target_seed_rule: OS entropy in evaluator after protocol freeze; target choices/coefficients held until final evaluation
calibration.rule: anonymous responses only; exhaustive one-feature scalar-kernel fits, stratified bounded two-feature fits; named calibrations and independently sampled in-language targets reported separately

boundaries.worker: Python audit-hook read/write allowlist; deny network/process launches; enforcement prevents accidental leakage, not a hostile-code security sandbox
boundaries.prime_labels: evaluator only; discovery summary metrics available to selector

assumptions: finite typed ASTs and supplied integer predicates restrict the search
scalar weights are rational; complex values arrive through generic inputs
finite matrix inverses have a declared dimension limit
small polynomial templates initialize nonlinear exploration
empirical prime contrast is not independent prime-distribution information
no analytic zeta/zero preservation primitive or convergence theorem is supplied
random synthetic targets are independently sampled within this language, not an external mathematical novelty benchmark
